title: Ancient Trees in South Africa: Places to Explore
meta_description: The country's stoutest baobab, a yellowwood that draws 80,000 visitors a year and a Cape Town fig where weddings are photographed. {trees} trees across {places} places in South Africa.
intro: The Sagole Baobab became South Africa's stoutest tree by default, once two larger baobabs, at Glencoe and Sunland, collapsed in 2009 and 2016. Its trunk is 32.89 metres round, and a reader who photographed it in Limpopo puts it at about 1,200 years old. South Africa's champion tree register lists the other two trees we map here. The Big Tree of Tsitsikamma, an Outeniqua yellowwood 36 metres tall, is reached by a short trail that more than 80,000 people walk every year, and its age is argued between 600 and more than 1,000 years. In Cape Town, a Moreton Bay fig in Arderne Gardens, a native of Australia, spreads its roots across the lawn on a scale that makes wedding parties look small, which is why the city calls it the Wedding Tree. It is listed as the largest tree in the Western Cape, 32.5 metres tall with a crown 44.3 metres across.
